messages.subject: inverse of negative log10 scale
parts:
Hi,

I am curious if there is a way to set the scale to the inverse of
-log10? Here is the formula I am trying to replicate:

10 ^ (-1) or equivalently the reciprocal of inverse of log10: 1 / (10 ^1)

I have been playing around with this (desired result is y = 0.1):

mydata <- data.frame(x = "a", y = 1)
qplot(x = x, y = y, data = mydata, geom = "point") +
scale_y_continuous(trans = c("reverse", "inverse", "log10"))

It's easy enough to transform by hand, so not really a big deal, but
it made me interested in on how using multiple transformations works.

Thanks,

Josh

--
Joshua Wiley

messages.author: 45a85351148578ad
messages.subject: RE: inverse of negative log10 scale
parts:
Hi Joshua,

I think you can create your own transformation using Trans.

Hope this helps,
fernando


library(ggplot2)
TransInvNegLog10 <- Trans$new("InvNegLog10", f = function(x) 10^(-x),
inverse = function(x) -log10(x), labels = function(x) x)
TransInvNegLog10b <- Trans$new("InvNegLog10b", f = function(x) 10^(-x),
inverse = function(x) -log10(x), labels = function(x)
bquote(10^.(-log10(x))))

mydata <- data.frame(x = c("a", "b"), y = c(1, 1.5))
qplot(x = x, y = y, data = mydata, geom = "point") +

scale_y_continuous(trans = c("InvNegLog10"))
